newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Women's groups call for inclusion on WTO agenda.
newsitem.headline: Women's groups call for inclusion on WTO agenda.

text.p: Women and their role in the world economy are being ignored by the World Trade Organisation (WTO) and should be on its agenda, a representative of a leading European action group said on Thursday.
"Economic policy making has an impact on women, yet there is absolutely no gender analysis for women's concerns being taken up whatsoever," Myriam Vander Stichele told Reuters in an interview.

Vander Stichele, research co-ordinator of the Amsterdam-based Transnational Institute and author of a new report on European Union trade policies for the Network Women in Development in Europe organisation, said 70 percent of the world's poorest 1.3 billion people were women.
She said women were at great risk from exploitation and that greater competitive pressures would expose them further still.

"As women we challenge the assumption that trade liberalisation is operating to the benefit of all and we ask that member states (of the WTO) investigate the real impact of these policies on women," said a statement released through the Transnational Institute.
"If export-oriented growth is based on exploited labour, how will this (economic benefit) trickle down through the rest of the economy?" Vander Stichele said.

She said the proposed social clause to the WTO ministerial declaration being backed by workers groups, including the International Confederation of Free Trade Unions, was a step forward, but did not go as far as women's groups would like.
Vander Stichele said she hoped that the impact of world trade policy on women would be on the agenda at the next WTO ministerial meeting in two years' time.
